title: Dynamic colony history and limits of static island architecture for Antarctic penguin demographic coupling
fit_rationale: The manuscript is explicitly biogeographical: it tests which forms of island information transfer from within-island demographic organization to site-level temporal response across Antarctica.

Part I provides a fixed-specification local-state association after provenance repair, with independent nest-level non-replication and a breeder-arrival route stopped by its frozen information gate; Part II tests transfer through static geographic descriptors across 104 site x species units and three Pygoscelis species.
The central contribution is response-specific transferability rather than a first demonstration that geography, habitat, synchrony or public information matters.

The non-confirmatory continental result is informative because the test and detectable-effect boundary are prespecified and because earlier Antarctic geography studies concern colony size, occurrence, spacing, clustering or long-term trends rather than the focal temporal-coupling response.
Externally subsidized breeding islands provide a general island-biogeographic setting in which terrestrial breeding structure and marine forcing are deliberately decoupled.

already_known: performance-based habitat selection/public-information hypotheses in colonial seabirds
a one-year breeding-success/growth association in Adelie penguins
physical habitat, snow and terrain effects on Adelie breeding sites
Antarctic penguin colony size/distribution relationships with social and physical geography
sea-ice associations with multidecadal Adelie population trends
new_here: denominator-separated short-lag history in a late-season colony-wide state after shared annual growth, prior size and persistent colony identity are controlled
metric specificity shown by independent nest-level non-replication
a predeclared cross-species test of whether static terrestrial island architecture predicts site-specific temporal coupling to shared annual forcing
a cross-scale synthesis that distinguishes local explanatory state from transferable macroecological structure without treating the two analyses as head-to-head effect-size competitors

editorial_risks: The Antarctic-wide primary p=0.0947 is non-confirmatory; the paper must be pitched as a transferability boundary, not a weak positive architecture effect.
The Palmer lag analysis is fixed-specification validation after provenance repair and cannot be presented as fully preregistered confirmation.
The late-season state is not generic reproductive success and public-information use is not demonstrated.
Part I and Part II have different responses and grains, so the synthesis must remain evidentiary rather than claiming dynamic state outperforms static place.
Main text is near the JBI word ceiling, so submission-stage additions require compensating cuts.
Post-result REPRO detectability/decomposition diagnostics may sharpen interpretation but cannot promote the failed independent nest-level endpoint into a positive validation.

HUMPOP is closed, not pending: 69 matched colony-seasons across 18 predictor seasons failed the prespecified minimum of 100, so no arrival coefficient was fit and the threshold cannot be lowered post hoc.
cover_letter_angle: A nested biogeographical test of information transfer: Palmer contains a fixed-specification local state association with an explicit provenance caveat, while independent nest-level validation is non-confirmatory and the preregistered arrival route stops at its information gate. Static breeding-island architecture likewise does not pass the predeclared Antarctic-wide test for temporal demographic coupling. The paper separates these responses from prior work on colony distribution, size, synchrony and long-term environmental trends.
prohibited_pitch: first evidence of public-information use in Adelie penguins
first Antarctic-wide test of penguin geography
the p=0.0947 interaction is marginally significant
the radius sign reversal proves scale dependence
Ross unpublished individual data confirm the mechanism

submission_target_decision.geb_branch_status: manuscript/integrated-v0.5-geb is archival only; no further scientific or editorial development should be made there unless JBI declines the manuscript.
submission_target_decision.rationale: The current paper is structured as an Aim/Location/Taxon biogeographical transferability test, and the JBI version already contains the frozen evidentiary boundaries, non-confirmatory continental result, and local-state interpretation.
